title: Secrets must not be placed in frontend code
learningObjectives: Explain secrets must not be placed in frontend code and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: Frontend JavaScript, HTML, source maps, and network requests are delivered to the user's browser and can be inspected. API keys intended to be public may have restricted scopes, but private keys, service credentials, signing secrets, and privileged tokens must remain on trusted servers.
understand.whyItMatters: Obfuscation and minification do not make a secret private. A leaked credential may be copied and abused, so use server-side secret storage, restricted credentials, rotation, and monitoring.
understand.analogy: Anything shipped to the browser is like a notice posted publicly; hiding the text in smaller print does not make it secret.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The example separates a public endpoint setting from credentials that must stay on the server. Even public provider keys need restrictions.

examples.explanation: The example separates a public endpoint setting from credentials that must stay on the server. Even public provider keys need restrictions.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates the API or security principle; browser permission or environment support may be required.

practise.guidedTask: Review a sample frontend config and classify each value as public configuration or secret. Move any privileged credential behind a server endpoint.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: Can a private API secret be protected by putting it in a minified frontend bundle?
options: No, browser-delivered code can be inspected
questions.answer: No, browser-delivered code can be inspected
questions.explanation: Minification does not provide confidentiality; frontend code and its runtime data are visible to users.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
